pageTitles.relaxkonos: RelaxKonOS — A modern remote workspace operating environment

pageDescriptions.home: RelaxKonOS is a cross-platform remote workspace operating environment with local UI rendering, persistent applications and server-managed workspaces. Not RDP, VNC or pixel streaming.

hero.title: Your server workspace, on desktop and mobile.
hero.lead: RelaxKonOS renders locally on Windows, macOS and Linux desktops and Android devices, using state synchronization to access your own server. Manage files, terminals, Docker, websites, certificates, Git, tunnels and proxies. Connect directly to Server, sign in to Server through an SSH tunnel, or use a separate SSH workbench.
hero.note: Not RDP. Not VNC. Not pixel streaming.

features.title: Designed around state, not screens.
features.lead: Every decision in RelaxKonOS follows the same idea: keep interaction with the user, keep durability on the server.

0.title: Local UI rendering
0.text: Desktop clients use Avalonia and Android uses Kotlin/Compose to render locally, keeping text and controls native and sharp.

1.title: Persistent applications
1.text: Terminal sessions, guarded workloads and remote services keep running on the server, so a dropped connection is never a lost session.

2.title: Clear boundaries
2.text: A dedicated protocol assembly owns every contract, so client, server and applications evolve independently.

3.title: Cross-platform
3.text: Desktop clients target Windows, macOS and Linux, alongside a native Android client. The download catalog lists the platforms and architectures actually published.

4.title: Security by delegation
4.text: Execution identity and file permissions come from the host OS. System and Alias sign-ins bind to the same user; privileged operations require separate authorization.

5.title: Extensible by design
5.text: Desktop packages implement IExternalRemoteApplication for scoped capabilities, windows and lifecycle. Android has a separate native application model.

apps.title: A complete workbench, not an empty desktop.
apps.lead: Desktop apps access server capabilities through shared contracts. Android provides native screens; availability depends on server mode, permissions and platform.

architecture.title: Three layers with one job each.
architecture.lead: A client that renders, a protocol that defines, and a server that owns the workspace.
architecture.clientText: The Avalonia desktop shell and Compose Android client handle presentation and input. Themes, credentials and SSH settings have local storage boundaries; workspace preferences sync through the server.
architecture.protocolText: REST routes, SignalR hub contracts and DTOs in a shared assembly with zero third-party dependencies.
architecture.serverText: Identity, workspace lifecycle, storage, synchronisation, remote runtime and platform services.
architecture.diagramCaption: The server manages state and services. It never captures or generates a desktop image.

platforms.title: Your workspace, on every device you use.
platforms.lead: The same workspace follows you between a workstation, a laptop and a server console.
platforms.windowsText: Avalonia desktop client; Windows hosts support LogonUser and ConPTY. See the download catalog for published architectures.
platforms.linuxText: Avalonia desktop client; Linux hosts support PAM/NSS and PTYs. Management features such as UFW depend on server mode and authorization.
platforms.macosText: The Avalonia desktop client uses WKWebView. Check the download catalog for published macOS packages.
platforms.serverNote: Servers target Linux and Windows. Client platform support, source implementation and published package availability are documented separately.
platforms.androidText: Native Kotlin/Compose client for phones and tablets, with Server/SSH connections, file transfers and service management. See the mobile guide for verification status.

security.title: Secure because it delegates, not because it reinvents.
security.lead: Sign-in methods can vary while execution remains bound to a host account. Both application authorization and host permissions must be satisfied.
security.identityText: System sign-in uses Windows LogonUser or Linux PAM. Alias uses an independent password hash bound to the same host user. The server does not persist system sign-in passwords.
security.permissionText: File operations run as the signed-in user. There is no second ACL to drift out of sync with the real one.
security.elevationText: Privileged actions use fixed Helper contracts. System-authenticated administrators are checked dynamically; ordinary users and Alias sessions explicitly authenticate a selected administrator. User mode disables elevation.

philosophy.title: Pixels are a poor interface to state.
philosophy.lead: A desktop image is an expensive, lossy way to express what a user wants. RelaxKonOS sends the intent instead.
philosophy.quote: Keep the interface on the device. Keep the workspace on the server.
philosophy.principle1Text: Anything that can be rendered on the client is rendered on the client.
philosophy.principle2Text: No business code issues raw HTTP or WebSocket calls.
philosophy.principle3Text: Users, permissions and existing tools belong to the operating system.
philosophy.principle4Text: Unsupported capabilities are reported, never faked.

os.title: Desktops beyond devices.
os.lead: RelaxKonOS combines an Avalonia desktop client and a Kotlin/Compose Android client with locally rendered interfaces, server-side workspace state and running services. Connect directly to Server, reach its loopback service through an SSH tunnel, or use an SSH terminal and SFTP workbench.
os.notRemoteText: RelaxKonOS is not RDP, VNC or a pixel streaming system, and it is not a browser-based management dashboard. The server never renders a desktop image; it manages the state and services that make a workspace durable.
os.capabilitiesTitle: Everything a server desktop needs, in one shell.
os.appsLead: Desktop apps share a runtime; Android provides separate native screens. Connections, host capabilities and permissions determine available actions.
os.archLead: A deliberately narrow contract keeps the layers independent and the failure modes obvious.
os.platformTitle: Client anywhere, server where it belongs.
os.securityLead: Three rules keep the security story short enough to audit.
os.extendLead: Desktop .roapp extensions use IExternalRemoteApplication and the scoped IExternalAppContext, packaged with the developer CLI. Built-in apps have a separate RemoteApplicationBase entry point.
os.statusTitle: Track implementation, verification and publication separately.
os.statusLead: Guides describe current source capabilities; downloads and release notes record published artifacts. Implemented source does not imply inclusion in a release or verification on every host.
os.statusItem1: Desktop shell, window manager and application runtime implemented
os.statusItem2: Server-side workspace, storage and synchronisation implemented
os.statusItem3: Service management is implemented; real-host verification for Docker, FRP, proxy and deployments is tracked in each guide
os.statusItem4: Windows/Linux x64 packages are in the catalog; other platforms list only verified published artifacts
os.limitsText: This site describes capabilities by their actual state: shipped, implemented but not yet verified, and not implemented are kept distinct. Some host-privileged features require explicit authorization at install time, and items whose real-environment acceptance is outstanding are never presented as fully available.

products.title: Software built around a clear architectural centre.
products.lead: RelaxKon builds workspace software where the interface stays local and the durable capabilities stay remote.
products.cardText: A cross-platform server workspace with local interfaces, persistent terminals and service management, supporting direct Server connections, SSH tunnel sign-in and a separate SSH workbench.
products.comingText: Additional workspace tools will be announced here as they become available.

downloads.title: Product downloads
downloads.lead: Every published build, by platform and architecture, with its size and checksum.
downloads.note: There are currently no downloadable artifacts. Check the catalog again later.
downloads.serverHint: Desktop clients, system servers and user-mode servers are different packages; Android uses signed APKs. Offline servers need only the appropriate server bundle.
downloads.clientRunHint: The client does not belong on the server. Download it to your own device, extract it, then run the command below.

userMode.title: Install under an ordinary Linux account (User Mode)
userMode.lead: User Mode requires no root and listens on 127.0.0.1. Choose Linux User Mode in Server Center; the client manages SSH forwarding. A *-user-server.zip package is required.
userMode.unavailable: No User Mode package is listed yet. Once available, select a local or server-side user-server ZIP in the client. System packages cannot substitute.

offline.title: Select an offline server package in the client
offline.lead: The target server needs no internet connection. Select a local ZIP in the client or a ZIP already copied to the server.
offline.stepOneText: On a connected machine, download the ZIP marked Server and retain its checksum for verification.
offline.stepTwoText: In Server Center, upload a local release ZIP or select a release ZIP already on the server.
offline.stepThreeText: Confirm the mode, port, directories, network, certificates and permissions. Check the operation receipt and health result.

packages.title: Packages and checksums
packages.lead: Use a direct archive for offline installs, controlled rollouts, or a manual checksum review.

downloads.androidHint: Download a published signed APK and confirm installation in Android. Updates must use the same signing certificate. AAB files are for store distribution, not direct installation.
downloads.androidUnavailable: No published Android APK is listed yet. Source implementation does not imply public package availability.

installFlow.title: Install the server from the client
installFlow.lead: Install the client, then connect to the target host through Server Center.
installFlow.stepOneText: Install the matching client on your computer or Android device.
installFlow.stepTwoText: Open Server Center, enter the SSH address, port and account, verify the host key and run preflight.
installFlow.stepThreeText: Choose the source and mode, configure ports, directories, network, certificates and permissions, then wait for health verification.
installFlow.maintenance: Use Server Center for updates, repair, rollback and uninstall. Uninstall retains data by default.

about.title: Build the workspace, not a screen stream.
about.lead: RelaxKon develops software around a simple premise: rich, responsive interfaces belong on the device in front of you, while workspaces, services and state should remain available across devices.
about.missionText: Server-side computing is powerful but its interfaces have stayed primitive. We think a desktop should be as responsive as the machine it runs on, and the work should outlive any single connection.
about.principle1Text: If the client can draw it, the client should draw it.
about.principle2Text: Every contract is written down in a shared protocol assembly.
about.principle3Text: Identity, permissions and existing tools belong to the host operating system.
about.project1Text: The website client: routing, layout, theme, runtime language switching and API clients.
about.project2Text: The content API: documentation, releases, downloads and FAQ served as Markdown and JSON.
about.project3Text: The product itself: desktop shell, window manager, application runtime, SDK and server.
about.licenseText: RelaxKonOS is published under the RelaxKonOS Non-Commercial Source-Available License. Non-commercial use, modification and study are welcome; commercial resale, redistribution or hosted offerings require a commercial licence.
about.contactText: For commercial licensing or partnership enquiries, reach out to the project maintainers.
